title: Bucyrus and Wynford gear up for 50th Battle for the Copper Kettle - NewsBreak
text:
By Zachary Holden ,
19 hours ago
BUCYRUS — Battle for the Copper Kettle week has arrived!
It hasn't been much of a battle for a long time, though, as Wynford leads rival Bucyrus 36-13 in the all-time series and the Royals come into Friday's Week 8 clash on a 28-game win streak over the Redmen. If you're good at math, Bucyrus led the overall series 13-8 before Wynford's nearly three-decade domination.
VOTE! Bucyrus Telegraph-Forum Football Player of the Week, Oct. 5
Breaking down Bucyrus But there's a believe in Bucyrus (3-4) that this could be the year that ends. The Redmen have already won as many games in seven weeks as they did the last four seasons combined (3-37) and it's the most prolific offense (260.9 yards and 15.1 points per game) since the 2019 team that finished 5-5.
And they're doing it with a ton of young talent leading the way.
Sophomore quarterback Isaac Makeever is completing 45.04% of his passes for 992 yards, eight touchdowns, and just two interceptions — the fewest in program history since the invention of the forward pass ( kidding) — and he also leads the team in rushing with 130 carries for 609 yards and four touchdowns.
His older brother Wyatt, a junior, is in the backfield with him more often than not having logged 36 attempts for 197 yards and three touchdowns rushing and caught a team-high 27 receptions for 344 yards and a touchdown. Junior Da'Shawn Cosey (13 catches, 308 yards, 4 TD), sophomore Cooper Kalb (6 catches, 135 yards), and senior Paten Deskins (5 catches, 96 yards, 2 TD) have been his other primary options out wide.
Defensively, the Redmen have been led by returning All-Ohio linebacker Hayden Butcher. The senior has 67 tackles, 16 for loss, five sacks, and one interception. The Makeevers have 53 tackles a piece with Wyatt adding eight tackles for loss and two interceptions, Isaac has two for loss and an interception; both are also linebackers.
Senior London Wade has five tackles for loss and half a sack as a defensive back, junior lineman Kayden Baxter has 20 tackles, four for loss, and 2.5 sacks, while Kalb, Cosey, and sophomore Ben Atwood each have a pick. Bucyrus boasts the second-most interceptions as a team in the Northern 10 with seven.
MORE: No. 1 spot in Jake Furr's football power poll to be settled on the field
Weighing up Wynford It has been an up-and-down year for the Royals (2-5) who opened with a win over still winless Cardington-Lincoln before dropping their next two games. They bounced back in Week 4, throttling county foe Buckeye Central for the 31st consecutive season, then ran into N10 title contenders Hopewell-Loudon and Mohawk.
Wynford put together one of its best performances of the season — only topped by 500-plus rushing yards against the Bucks — last weekend against rival Colonel Crawford. Despite coming up short 33-27, the Royals rushed for 324 yards and scored their third-most points this season; in the four previous losses the team mustered just 28 total points.
Sophomore quarterback Braylon Wells leads the league in rushing with 1,100 yards and 13 touchdowns on 143 carries, averaging 157.1 yards per game on the ground. He has thrown for just 172 yards and a touchdown with two interceptions, but leads the team defensively with 46 tackles, one interception, and a forced fumble.
Complementing him in the run game is senior Deegan Lutz, who has logged 89 attempts for 490 yards and five touchdowns while also leading the team with 62 yards on five catches. Junior Gage Massey (6 catches, 60 yards, TD), senior Eli Cooper (6 catches, 45 yards); senior tight end Gavin Koehler (3 catches, 5 yards) round out the receiving corps.
On defense the Royals have been very balanced, boasting seven players with more than 30 tackles — senior Zaiden Zier has 39, Koehler 37, senior Victor Arellano and junior Memphis Routson 36 each, Massey 35, Cooper and junior Jamison Crall 30 apiece — along with sophomores Wyatt Stahl (28) and Levi Webb (22), and Lutz's 21 as the bulk of Wynford's 406 total tackles.
Routson has six for loss and 1.5 sacks, Crall five for loss and 1.5 sacks, Lutz 4.5 for loss and three sacks, Stahl four for loss and half-a-sack. Wells has the team's lone interception of the season, Routson has forced two and recovered two fumbles, and Arellano is 16-of-17 kicking extra points boasting the third-best conversion rate in the league.
MOAC TITLE BOUT: What gives Shelby, Ontario the edge in Week 8 clash?
Iconic Copper Kettle clashes Before Friday's 50th edition of the Battle for the Copper Kettle, let's take a stroll down memory lane at some of the best games these bitter rivals have had over the last half-century.
2022: Wynford 20, Bucyrus 14 Just before this senior class got into high school was the last time we saw a legitimately close game . In fact, Bucyrus had the ball and a chance to take the lead with under two minutes to go, but the Royals defense held pat and hit the quarter-century streak mark.
2021: Wynford 72, Bucyrus 20 The most lopsided result in the history of the rivalry — matched two years later (70-18) — was also the second-most points the Royals have scored this century. And believe it or not, it was a one-possession game midway through the second quarter.
Wynford jumped out to a 22-0 lead in the first before back-to-back Bucyrus touchdowns made it 22-14. You can do the math from there ... 50-7 in favor of the Royals thanks to a monster game from Jaron Filliater who finished with seven catches for 106 yards and a touchdown with two interceptions on defense. Kaden Blair also rushed in a trio of touchdowns. It would go on to be the final win for legendary coach Gabe Helbert in the rivalry, exiting a perfect 10-0 against the Redmen.
2013: Wynford 41, Bucyrus 40 In the conversation for most thrilling game in the rivalry, this one came down to a failed two-point conversion by Bucyrus in the final minutes. Current Ontario coach Aaron Eckert elected to go for two — because why wouldn't you in a rivalry you haven't won in ages — and Helbert was able to let out a sigh of relief by the final whistle.
Brock Williamson led the Royals with 234 yards of offense passing for two touchdowns and rushing in a third, Cole Murtiff tossed a trio of touchdowns for the Redmen finishing with 219 yards passing.
2007: Wynford 55, Bucyrus 14 The last time both teams were undefeated coming into the Battle for the Copper Kettle. Wynford racked up 654 yards of offense, led by five rushing touchdowns by Nate Etler. It was previously the largest victory margin of the rivalry until 2021 and 2023. The Royals went on to go a perfect 10-0 and win the North Central Conference before falling to Lima Central Catholic in the playoffs while Bucyrus was 9-1 and missed out on the postseason. Only eight teams qualified back then, and the Redmen were 13th in Region 14.
1997: Bucyrus 18, Wynford 13 The last time Bucyrus won, Princess Diana was still alive. Benji Brant rushed for 162 yards with a 95-yard a touchdown, and Steve Binnix and Josh Weiler also found pay dirt for the Redmen. Bucyrus finished 8-2 that season under eventual OHSFCA Hall of Fame coach Doug Frye. It was the eight consecutive season the program finished at .500 or better.
1983: Bucyrus 13, Wynford 10 An iconic game in the series that featured the first made field goal, christened Bucyrus' new football field and was won on the final play.
Wynford scored first on a Derek Wirebaugh 1-yard rush that was immediately responded to with a kickoff return from Bucyrus' Dana Foght. The Royals then made history when David Cooper drilled a 20-yard field goal to take the lead before the Redmen walked it off on a Mike Hunter-to-Todd Ernsberger 33-yard strike with 0:00 on the clock — later dubbed the Kettle Katch.
1977: Bucyrus 22, Wynford 14 The game that started it all! Back at Lane Street Field in the regular season finale, Bucyrus stormed out to a 22-0 lead and watched its new rival score twice in the fourth quarter to make for an interesting ending.
Scott Pensinger scored the first (and second) touchdown in the Battle for the Copper Kettle from 39 (and 38) yards out, ending the game with 168 yards on 17 carries. Tim Schifer scored Wynford's first touchdown in the rivalry with Steve Campbell rushing in the second.
